_readme: Seedance 2.5 — the clip model (Higgsfield API; BytePlus ModelArk is the maker's own door). Filled 2026-10-26 from the maker's prompt guide, same shape as gpt-image-2.5.json so one library, one slice renderer and one checker serve both.

The field-level contract (which field a request carries) stays in tools/video-production/machine/model-inputs.json (stations motion, talking). What the clip prompt must look like is built by tools/video-production/machine/seedance_prompt.py and explained in tools/video-production/SEEDANCE-INPUTS.md.

The rulebook for the Seedance 2.5 clip: every input with its limit and our job, so the chain always gets the best image-to-video. Every row carries its source; every entry is status draft until it is approved. No brand, product, person or format word appears in this file.
label: Seedance 2.5

house.takes: up to the configured maximum number of attempts (default 3 on Seedance, then the Kling backup as the last rung); each scored; the best-scoring one kept, a tie to the later, flagged below_criteria if it did not pass (V34)
house.duration: a talking take: its read × 1.15 + 0.6 s, rounded up (room for the model's own pauses); a silent one: its window; 4 to 30 s, the model's own range (the old 10 s cap was the retired Omni model's, removed 2026-10-28)

limits.note: A first-frame or last-frame ROLE locks the output to that picture's aspect and cannot sit beside audio on Higgsfield; a picture called 'the first frame' in the words is allowed and followed approximately.

inputs.name: prompt
inputs.what: The words: bound files, one sentence, timeline, constants.
inputs.allowed: no stated limit; the shortest prompt that fully says the shot

inputs.name: image (first frame)
inputs.what: The approved start picture, named 'Image 1 is the first frame'.
inputs.allowed: 1 to 30 images; 1 to 8 subjects is the stable range

inputs.name: image (other roles)
inputs.what: A face, product, room or look reference, each bound by number and job.
inputs.allowed: same pool as above; separate views, never a collage
inputs.we_send: none in the chain; the bench can add them to test

inputs.name: image (last frame)
inputs.allowed: role last_frame (locks aspect) or named in the words; not beside audio on Higgsfield
inputs.we_send: silent clips only, only when different from the first

inputs.name: video (reference)
inputs.what: Motion, camera or style from a clip; says what it is for and what to ignore.
inputs.allowed: up to 10, 30 s together, 5 to 10 s each works best; its subtitles and voices override the prompt
inputs.we_send: the swipe's blurred clips, up to 3 of 2 to 8 s, 'motion and camera only'
inputs.use: yes where the swipe's movement is the point

inputs.name: audio (reference)
inputs.what: A voice, music or rhythm; dialogue audio doubles as the speech.
inputs.we_send: the line's locked read, one clip, bound as the speaker's voice

inputs.name: aspect_ratio
inputs.allowed: any from 0.4 to 2.5 on 2.5; fixed by a first/last-frame role or an edit source

inputs.name: generate_audio
inputs.we_send: true on talking clips, false on silent

inputs.name: output_format
inputs.allowed: mp4; mov keeps colour and sound consistency in edits and extensions

structure.rule: Name every image, video and audio by its upload number and job: 'Image 1 is the first frame', 'Video 1 is for camera movement only', 'Audio 1 is the voice'. Upload in the order the subjects first appear.
Then one summary sentence: subject, place, event, style, camera.

A timeline in whole-second windows that touch, or 'Shot N'. One primary change per window; too little and it improvises, too much and it adds cuts or skips the action. Do not time fast repeated actions.
structure.ours: windows of at least 2.5 s, two actions at most

structure.rule: End with what stays constant (camera, place, light, sound), then the few negatives.
Say what you want. Negatives are supported for subtitles and audio ('no subtitles', 'no BGM').
Name the shot size and ONE dominant move per shot ('slow push-in at eye level'); give an unusual term a plain explanation.
structure.ours: CAMERA phrases from the shot's camera_move

structure.rule: When a reference is accurate, say to use it; do not describe it again.
structure.ours: 'keep this exact person, face, clothing, props, room and light'

structure.rule: Name who speaks; keep a line's delivery next to it as 'Character's line (emotion): words'. Do not repeat dialogue words or attach tone notes to single words: it triggers subtitles.
structure.ours: the words live in Audio 1 only

structure.rule: Replace an emotion label with a trigger, a visible physical response and a delay. A strong emotion word can make the eyes glow.
structure.ours: the shot's face and gestures; the emotion label is not sent

structure.rule: Name the visual bridge across a cut or join; describe the boundary state (pose, prop, light, camera, motion direction) on both sides of an extension.
Give each file one job and state what it must NOT pass on; bind each subject one by one, not 'images 1 to 4 respectively'.
structure.ours: VIDEO_LINE and the image role lines

structure.rule: A task that mixes several references and edits is unstable: split it into simpler passes.
structure.ours: one picture, one voice, one clip

avoid.text: Typing the line beside its audio: it triggers burnt-in subtitles and says the words twice.
Strong emotion labels ('fanatical', 'extremely shocked'): they can light the eyes or overact.
Vague words ('cinematic', 'epic reveal', 'dynamic camera', 'make it emotional and beautiful').
Long generic blacklists: they compete with the scene.
Several events or exact timestamps in one short window: extra cuts, skipped actions.
A reference video with subtitles, voices or music you do not want: they override the prompt unless rejected.
'Based on all references', an unused file, or a mapping that lives only inside a picture.
A locked tripod and aggressive handheld in the same beat; one continuous take with five cuts.
Words the model must spell: it misspells; give them as a reference picture or lay them on later.
A first/last-frame role beside audio references on Higgsfield (the 422).

history.said: we are also going to do this for seedance too so we always get the best quality image and image to video

history.about: every clip is made at 480p and upscaled on this Mac
